title: Kaplansky decomposition into countably generated projectives
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P$ be a projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. There exist a set $I$, projective $R$-modules $P_i$ for $i\in I$, and an $R$-linear isomorphism $\bigoplus_{i\in I}P_i\cong P$, such that every $P_i$ is countably generated: it has an at most countable subset whose finite $R$-linear combinations exhaust $P_i$. Here $\bigoplus_{i\in I}P_i$ is the module of families $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ with $x_i\in P_i$ and only finitely many nonzero coordinates, with componentwise operations. No finite-generation hypothesis is imposed on $P$.

proof.text: By the direct-summand characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], choose a free $R$-module $F$ and $R$-linear maps $i:P\to F$ and $s:F\to P$ with $s\circ i=\mathrm{id}_P$. By the basis description of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], $F\cong\bigoplus_{j\in J}R$; each copy of $R$ is generated by $1$, so $F$ is a direct sum of countably generated $R$-modules (the empty basis case gives the zero module).

source.place: Tag 058Y, theorem-projective-direct-sum, proof: a projective module is a direct summand of a free module; Tags 05CE and 00C2 for the characterizations of projective and free modules

proof.text: Apply the Kaplansky direct-summand theorem [lem-trf-projective-kaplansky-direct-summand] to the direct-sum decomposition of $F$ from step 1 and the retract $P\subset F$. It yields an index set $I$, countably generated $R$-modules $Q_i$ for $i\in I$, and an $R$-linear isomorphism $\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i\cong P$.

For each $i$, the canonical inclusion and projection of $Q_i$ in the direct sum, transported across the isomorphism $\bigoplus_iQ_i\cong P$, give maps $Q_i\to P\to Q_i$ whose composite is the identity. Since $P$ is projective, [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand] (the direct-summand closure of projectivity) shows that every $Q_i$ is projective. Renaming $Q_i$ as $P_i$ gives the required family of countably generated projective modules and the stated isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem exists_directSum_countablyGenerated_projective (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Projective R P] : ∃ (I : Type v) (Q : I → Type v) (_ : ∀ i, AddCommGroup (Q i)) (_ : ∀ i, Module R (Q i)), (∀ i, Module.Projective R (Q i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ s : Set (Q i), s.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R s = ⊤) ∧ Nonempty ((⨁ i : I, Q i) ≃ₗ[R] P)
